rv.q: It’s a joyride into the construction of identity, and one with unexpected emotional resonance as it charts Ann’s well of loneliness, and all our desires to leave some mark upon the world, however small.
RoosevElvis is not funny enough to carry this Brit through all its US references: I could have done with a glossary.

However, The TEAM’s newest devised work, currently transferred from Brooklyn to Sloane Square, is an extremely charming, intimate evening at the theatre that can warm the hearts of even the most cynical.
It is, amongst other things, one of the best portraits of depression I've ever seen: as Ann, King's face hangs slack, as if even expressions require too much energy.

At times it’s a bit muddled and with so much crammed into 100 minutes, maybe a little pruning would have resulted in a more cohesive message and a more satisfying theatrical experience for the audience.

cn.t: Critics largely praise RoosevElvis for its bold gender-bending concept and intellectual rigor, though some find it uneven. The TEAM's high-concept two-hander earns mostly strong notices for its ambition, if not always its execution.
